findings.title: The hidden-remote-prflx fallback labels internet sessions 'lan' whenever this machine has a private host address
findings.claim: The R1-F1 fix (which follows my round-1 suggestion) labels a remote prflx candidate with no readable address 'lan' whenever the local selected candidate is host at a private address. That inference does not hold. Almost every home or office PC's host candidate is private (192.168.x or 10.x), and a NAT translates it on the way out. So a private local host address says nothing about where the far side is. On the internet path (plan ii adds STUN/TURN through `iceServers`), Chromium reports the remote as peer-reflexive whenever its connectivity check arrives before its srflx candidate is signalled, or when it sits behind a symmetric NAT. It also hides that remote address. The pair is then host(private)/prflx(hidden), and the new rule calls it 'lan'. My round-1 fix traded one wrong label for its mirror image.
findings.evidence: plan L61 (Decision 1: 'a local host candidate at a private address means the far side reached a private address, so lan'); plan L315 (`far = ... judged(remote) ?? (local.candidateType === 'host' && localAddress(at(local)) ? 'lan' : null)`); plan L181 (the test pins `rtcRoute(c('host', '192.168.1.5'), c('prflx'))` as 'lan'); src/network/rtc/peer.ts:L31,L195 (the peer takes `iceServers`, empty in plan i's tests at plan L168, filled by plan ii)
findings.why: An internet session labelled 'lan' fails the internet checklist's transport check. It also judges the Helm's held p95 against the 150 ms LAN limit instead of 250 ms, which can trip H-2c falsely (fallback check 1, plan L94). The one-PC smoke cannot show this, because there the pair is host/host.
findings.fix: Only trust the local-side inference when it is sound. Pass `rtcRoute` whether the attempt was configured with no ICE servers (`servers.length === 0` in peer.ts). With no STUN/TURN, neither side gathers srflx or relay candidates, so a hidden remote prflx means a direct LAN check, and 'lan' is fair. With ICE servers configured, return null (unknown). Reword Decision 1 to match. Update the L181 test, and add a case where a private local host plus a hidden remote prflx with ICE servers configured gives null.

prior.note: A readable prflx address on either side is now judged correctly (plan L310-L316, tests L178-L188), and a hidden remote with no private local host gives null rather than 'internet'. But the new fallback, a private local host means 'lan', mislabels internet sessions whose remote appears as prflx: see the new finding. The fix was the one I suggested in round 1, and it is unsound on the internet path.

formatReport (plan L1789-L1801) evaluates the targets over the claimed rooms only, labels the line, and lists unclaimed and missing rooms. With no checklist it prints a warning. The tests at plan L1551-L1554 and L1615-L1617 match the fixture: room A has 3 rounds, A plus B have 4.

The test awaits flush() after attach (plan L912). The samples are [90,60,40,50,70] with an expected median of 60 (L916-L921). Each step is 1001 ms, at least LINK_POLL_MS (L1139, L1161), so every sample is polled.
The sort is now by round index, then startedAtIso (plan L1696-L1698), so every round k-1 is placed before round k whichever clock wrote it.
The copy loop is in try/catch with `failure ??= 'record copy failed'`, before runtime.dispose() and the temp-root removal (plan L1993-L2003).

oneNetwork (plan L1775-L1779) judges sessions on one known network. The test (L1586-L1590) covers lan s1, internet s2 (the fixture has room B as internet, L1541), mixed s3 and unknown s4. Decision 9 states the reason.

The peer keeps `rtt` as null for a missing or out-of-range currentRoundTripTime (plan L383-L384), and linkFigures returns it (L388). The controller sends stats only with a route and a non-null RTT (L457-L458). The test pins the no-RTT case (L222). diagnostics() still returns 0 for its existing callers.

verified: The rtcRoute truth table matches every new test case at plan L178-L190. localAddress(undefined) returns false (plan L295), so `c('host')` with a hidden prflx remote gives null.
The controller rig's `set('lan', null)` type-checks: rttMs is declared `number | null` (plan L205), and the default parameter only applies to undefined.

evaluateFallbacks still covers all rooms for check 1 while the live targets cover only claimed rooms. The CLI test's 'H-2c starts: yes' (plan L1618) follows from room B's 300 ms guest-Helm p95 against the internet limit.
Task 4 Step 2's expected output now includes the no-checklist warning (plan L2019), consistent with formatReport L1800-L1801.
The gates text (plan L1879, L1883) matches the revised Decisions 1 and 8.
not_verified: Whether Chromium exposes the real address of local host candidates in getStats when mDNS obfuscation is on. If it hides them too, the local-side inference rarely fires. I did not check this against Chromium sources.

Which candidate type Chromium reports for the selected pair's local candidate behind a NAT (host vs srflx). This decides how often the new finding's mislabel occurs in practice, and I could not check it read-only.
